title: PREX package manifest (one package, every ecosystem it ships to)
$comment: Shaped after the MCP registry's server.json, which solved the same problem for MCP servers: one document naming a thing plus the several package managers it can be obtained from. Three deliberate differences. Integrity is a PREX Digest, not a bare sha256 hex string, so the algorithm is stated rather than assumed. A distribution names a registryId from a Registry Definition, not just a base URL, so an external registry provider is identified rather than located. And provenance is evidence PREX already produces — snapshot, receipt, trust tier, semantic loss — not a publisher-supplied blob nobody checked.

name.$comment: The name a human uses. Ecosystem-specific spellings live on each distribution, because npm's @scope/name and NuGet's Scope.Name are the same package under different rules.

version.$comment: The release this manifest describes. Exact: a manifest naming a range describes no particular thing, and could not be pinned or verified.

registries.$comment: Registry Definitions this manifest's distributions refer to, carried inline so a consumer can resolve registryId without a second lookup. External registry providers are first class here.

distributions.$comment: server.json calls these `packages`. One entry per ecosystem this release ships to.

purlType.$comment: The PURL type, which PREX already uses as the ecosystem's identity everywhere else. server.json's registryType is the same idea with a private vocabulary; reusing purl means no second naming scheme to keep in step.

identifier.$comment: The name this ecosystem knows the package by, spelled the ecosystem's way.

exactPurl.$comment: The canonical PREX identity. Derivable from purlType/identifier/version, and stated so a consumer never has to re-derive it and get the encoding rules wrong.

registryId.$comment: Which authority publishes it. A base URL says where to look; this says who is answering, which is what a policy can pin.

digest.$comment: sha256 over the archive bytes — PREX identity, algorithm stated.

runtimeHint.$comment: How this is ordinarily run without installing it, as server.json spells it: npx, uvx, dnx, docker.

NativeIntegrity.$comment: The value the ecosystem's own lockfile pins with, kept beside the PREX digest rather than instead of it: npm SRI, NuGet base64 sha512, Cargo sha256 hex. A consumer writing a native lockfile needs this exact form; a consumer verifying identity needs the digest.

serviceIndex.$comment: Where the Registry Definition itself can be fetched, so an external provider is discoverable rather than hardcoded.

definitionDigest.$comment: The Registry Definition this manifest was built against. A registry that later advertises different capabilities is a different answer, and this is what makes that visible.

Provenance.$comment: What is known about where this came from, and what was actually checked. server.json carries publisher-provided metadata; this carries the artefacts PREX itself produced, so a consumer can tell a claim from a verification.

receiptDigest.$comment: The resolution receipt this manifest's versions came from. Without it the versions are an assertion; with it they are checkable.

verified.$comment: Which claims were checked when this was produced, rather than merely recorded. An empty list is an honest answer.
